topics.topic: Define the State 5 contracts and operation-count impact for system_clock.utc_now and system_clock.monotonic_seconds
questions: What are the State 5 contracts for `system_clock.utc_now` and `system_clock.monotonic_seconds`, including their callers, inputs, outputs, errors, observable effects and state impact, and is the operation count now 102 rather than 100?
What are the State 5 contracts for `system_clock.utc_now` and `system_clock.monotonic_seconds`, including their callers, inputs, outputs, errors and effects, and does the operation count become 102?

Are utc_now and monotonic_seconds public State 5 operations, and if so what are their exact inputs, outputs, errors, effects and caller lists; if they are not, how do the newly listed time-reading modules obtain time from system_clock?

quotes:
One public operation per State 3 capability (100; the eight operations of the
email challenges and their delivery left with them on 2026-11-07,
`00_product.md` R0-23), each proven by the State 4
flows `50_api_plan.json` names.

Only `system_clock` reads the host clocks (A28). An operation
  that needs the current instant takes one wall reading from it and reuses
  it; the transport guard takes the elapsed reading for the viewer-entry
  window from it. No other module reads a host clock.
judgement.divergence: One implementer exposes `utc_now` and `monotonic_seconds` as the two additional public operations required by the one-operation-per-capability rule, giving State 5 a 102-operation surface; another keeps the stated 100-operation surface and invents a private clock interface or direct dependency. State 6 generation and module-dependency checks observe different callable surfaces and caller graphs.
judgement.why: The newly added State 3 capabilities have no State 5 operation entries fixing their callers, inputs, outputs, errors, effects, or state impact, while State 5 still asserts a complete 100-operation surface.

witness.initial: The design contains the new `system_clock` module and its two candidate capabilities, while State 5 declares a complete 100-operation public surface.
events: A State 6 author generates contracts for every State 3 candidate capability.
The author reaches `system_clock.utc_now` and `system_clock.monotonic_seconds`, for which State 5 supplies no operation entries.
outcomes: The author treats the one-operation-per-capability statement as controlling, creates two additional public contracts, and produces 102 public operations.
The author treats the stated count and enumerated State 5 entries as controlling, creates no public clock contracts, and leaves consumers to use an invented private clock interface.

topics.topic: Define the scope and cardinality of the A28 one-clock-reading-per-request rule
questions: Does “one reading per request” mean one shared wall-clock reading for the whole HTTP request, or one reading for each operation/call that needs time?
Does “request” mean one HTTP request, one application operation, or one call to the clock source when several operations and the audit writer run during one HTTP request?

Does “one reading per request” mean one reading for the entire HTTP request, one reading for each use-case operation, or one host-clock read for each call to utc_now, especially when a mutation and audit_writer both need a time?

quotes: append_audit: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.

_authorize_project_operation: [BEHAVIOR] MUST read the current UTC time once per operation, by one call of utc_now, and use that single instant for every timestamp it writes and every current-time comparison it makes; it MUST NOT read a host clock itself.

It MUST supply _record_viewer_entry_attempt with one reading of monotonic_seconds per entry attempt, a clock that cannot move backwards, never with wall-clock time and never with a host clock read directly, so that adjusting the system clock cannot widen the window or discard recorded attempts.
judgement.why: The later notes define clock reads per operation, give `append_audit` its own call, and separately require one monotonic reading per viewer-entry attempt, rather than one shared reading for an entire HTTP request.

topics.topic: Define completed_work_value when planned work exists without a SectionProgress record
questions: For a section with planned work but no `SectionProgress`, must `completed_work_value` be numeric zero or explicitly unavailable?

For a section with planned work but no SectionProgress record, is completed_work_value a confirmed numeric zero or unavailable/missing, and what assertion is required to close INV-044 rather than merely record the current zero?

quotes: build_progress_view: [RETURN_SHAPE] MUST project active-budget sections, manual completion values, per-section completed work, total, and weighted overall progress. For a section with no progress row, completion_percent remains None and MUST NOT be zero-filled, because the absence of a measurement is not a measurement of zero; completed_work_value for that section is Decimal zero, because the field is a required Decimal and no work has been earned. The two are different answers to different questions and MUST NOT be conflated.
judgement.why: The later notes explicitly distinguish missing completion measurement from earned work and require `completion_percent` to be absent while `completed_work_value` is decimal zero.

topics.topic: Define how provider or forbidden recognition fields reach and are rejected by create_expense_from_recognition
questions: What input reaches the direct operation check for forbidden recognition status/provider fields, and which layer and declared exception must refuse it?

How can create_expense_from_recognition itself receive and refuse a provider-carrying result when its State 5 input is the already-decoded ConfirmedRecognitionPublication model, which has no provider field and whose provider fields are said never to cross the boundary?

quotes: create_expense_from_recognition_endpoint: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST accept its non-path application input only from the explicit RecognitionExpenseCreateRequest JSON body, reject unknown body fields through the shared frozen model policy, and delegate payload.publication and payload.allocations; none of those fields may be interpreted as a query parameter.

create_expense_from_recognition: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST accept only confirmed complete normalized input whose contract_version is in the supported OCR contract versions [1], validate explicit allocations, apply R8 replay before mutation, and atomically insert one Expense plus one ExpenseDocument plus allocations and AuditAction.EXPENSE_CREATE audit.

_project_expense_intake: [FIELD_PROJECTION] MUST project only confirmed normalized business fields, recognized_document_id, intake_fingerprint inputs, file_ref, and explicit allocations; it MUST NOT project confidence, provider fields, or raw responses.
judgement.why: The later notes assign rejection of undeclared provider fields to strict request-model decoding and constrain the operation to an already decoded confirmed publication whose projection excludes provider data.

topics.topic: Define validate_project_reference behavior when Registry returns exists=false
questions: When Registry returns a successful decoded ProjectValidationResult with exists=false, must validate_project_reference return that result for its caller to classify, or must the gateway itself refuse with RegistryBoundaryError/not_found?

quotes:
`ProjectValidationResult` decoded from the response, whose identity is the
requested one.

`RegistryBoundaryError` for timeout, transport, HTTP, schema or identity
failure.

A decoded validation answer is returned as it is and read by
its caller as A5 says; the two readings of A5 agree, because the Registry
sets `is_active = true` exactly when `status` is `active` (Registry v1
`validate_project_reference`).
judgement.why: The gateway returns a successfully decoded `ProjectValidationResult`, including `exists=false`, while its caller classifies that result; only transport, HTTP, schema, or identity failures raise `RegistryBoundaryError`.

topics.topic: Identify the exact client-supplied Registry context fields that request decoding must reject
questions: Which exact request fields count as client-supplied Registry context and must be rejected, without rejecting the required project identity and legitimate portal-owned fields?

quotes: create_expense_from_recognition_endpoint: [SECURITY_BOUNDARY] MUST accept its non-path application input only from the explicit RecognitionExpenseCreateRequest JSON body, reject unknown body fields through the shared frozen model policy, and delegate payload.publication and payload.allocations; none of those fields may be interpreted as a query parameter.

_authorize_project_operation: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST run its guard steps in this order with the first failure winning: valid session (staff and viewer principals only; a service principal has no session), active principal, project access, required capability, Registry lifecycle; it MUST resolve persisted revocation/current-principal state, ignore client Registry context, validate the same UUID server-side, and reject inactive mutation targets.
judgement.why: The later notes define the boundary structurally: the declared request-model fields, including the required project identity inside the publication, are accepted; every undeclared field is rejected, and authorization ignores any client Registry context.
